name: TSMC
specialization: Pure-play foundry — leading-edge logic and advanced packaging (CoWoS)
description: TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company) is the world's largest pure-play foundry, fabricating chips designed by other companies on its leading-edge logic processes and advanced CoWoS packaging. Headquartered in Hsinchu, Taiwan, it was founded in 1987 by Morris Chang, who pioneered the dedicated-foundry model — a company that manufactures silicon but designs none of its own products. That bet created the modern fabless ecosystem and now makes TSMC the critical supplier for Apple, NVIDIA, AMD and most leading-edge chips.

name: Samsung Electronics (Device Solutions)
specialization: DRAM/NAND memory, foundry, and advanced logic
description: Samsung's Device Solutions division is a vertically integrated manufacturer (IDM) spanning DRAM and NAND memory, a contract foundry, and advanced logic. Founded as part of Samsung Electronics in 1969 in Suwon, South Korea, it grew from consumer electronics into the world's largest memory maker and the only credible leading-edge foundry alternative to TSMC.

name: SK Hynix
description: SK Hynix is a South Korean memory manufacturer specializing in DRAM and NAND flash, and the leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI accelerators. Founded in 1983 as Hyundai Electronics, it became Hynix after the late-1990s Korean chip consolidation and was acquired by the SK Group in 2012. Its early lead in HBM made it NVIDIA's primary memory partner during the AI boom.

name: Micron Technology
description: Micron Technology is the only U.S.-based maker of DRAM and NAND memory and a growing HBM supplier. Founded in 1978 in the basement of a Boise, Idaho dental office, it survived decades of brutal memory cycles through acquisitions — Texas Instruments' memory unit, Elpida, and Inotera — to become one of the three remaining DRAM giants alongside Samsung and SK Hynix.

name: Intel
specialization: x86 CPUs, leading-edge IDM, and foundry services (IFS)
description: Intel is an integrated device manufacturer that designs and builds x86 CPUs and is now opening its fabs to outside customers through Intel Foundry Services. Founded in 1968 in Santa Clara by Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore, it defined the PC and data-center processor era. After ceding process leadership to TSMC, it is attempting a costly comeback in both manufacturing and foundry.

name: NVIDIA
specialization: GPU and AI accelerators; data-center networking (fabless)
description: NVIDIA is a fabless designer of GPUs and AI accelerators plus the CUDA software and networking that surround them; it outsources all manufacturing to TSMC and its packaging and memory partners. Founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem to build graphics chips for gaming, it repositioned the GPU as the engine of modern AI and became the most valuable chip company in the world.

name: AMD
description: AMD is a fabless designer of CPUs, GPUs and adaptive (FPGA) silicon for PCs, data centers and embedded markets. Founded in 1969 by Jerry Sanders and former Fairchild engineers, it spent decades as Intel's x86 challenger. Spinning off its fabs into GlobalFoundries in 2009 and acquiring Xilinx in 2022 turned it into a fabless powerhouse competing in both CPUs and AI GPUs.

name: Apple
specialization: Mobile and PC SoC design (fabless); systems and services
description: Apple designs its own mobile and PC system-on-chips (the A- and M-series) in-house but is fabless, relying on TSMC for fabrication and Asian partners for assembly. Founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne, it began building custom silicon after acquiring P.A. Semi in 2008 and is consistently TSMC's largest customer and first adopter of each new process node.

name: Qualcomm
specialization: Mobile SoC, RF, and automotive silicon (fabless)
description: Qualcomm is a fabless designer of mobile SoCs (Snapdragon), modems and RF front-ends, and a major holder of wireless patents. Founded in 1985 in San Diego by Irwin Jacobs and Andrew Viterbi, it commercialized CDMA cellular technology and now sources advanced chips from both TSMC and Samsung's foundry.

name: Broadcom
specialization: Networking ASIC, custom silicon, and infrastructure semiconductors
description: Broadcom designs networking ASICs, custom accelerators for hyperscalers, and a broad range of infrastructure semiconductors, and also sells enterprise software. The modern company was formed when Avago — itself descended from Hewlett-Packard's 1961 semiconductor unit — acquired Broadcom Corporation in 2016. It is a key partner for cloud companies building their own AI chips.

name: MediaTek
description: MediaTek is a Taiwanese fabless designer of mobile, connectivity and smart-device SoCs, and one of the largest smartphone chip vendors by volume. Spun out of UMC in 1997 and based in Hsinchu, it built its business on cost-effective, highly integrated chipsets and relies on TSMC for leading-edge wafers.

name: UMC
description: United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) is a Taiwanese pure-play foundry focused on mature and specialty process nodes. Founded in 1980 as Taiwan's first semiconductor company — a spin-off of the government's ITRI — it predates TSMC and competes today on trailing-edge and specialty capacity rather than the leading edge.

name: SMIC
specialization: China domestic foundry (mature to mid-node; leading-edge export-constrained)
description: Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC) is China's largest foundry and the spearhead of its domestic chip ambitions. Founded in 2000 in Shanghai by Richard Chang, it serves Chinese and global fabless customers on mature-to-mid nodes. U.S. export controls cap its access to EUV and the most advanced tools, constraining its leading-edge progress.

name: GlobalFoundries
description: GlobalFoundries is a foundry specializing in mature and specialty nodes — RF, power and automotive — rather than the leading edge. Created in 2009 when AMD spun off its manufacturing, and later merged with Singapore's Chartered Semiconductor and IBM's fab unit, it is now a U.S.-headquartered, globally operated supplier serving customers who need reliable, differentiated capacity.

name: ASE Technology Holding
description: ASE Technology Holding is the world's largest provider of outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) and advanced packaging. Founded in 1984 in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, it packages and tests finished wafers for fabless and IDM customers. As chip performance increasingly depends on packaging, ASE sits at a fast-growing chokepoint of the supply chain.

name: Amkor Technology
description: Amkor Technology is a leading OSAT firm providing packaging and test services, with most operations across Asia and a new advanced-packaging fab planned in Arizona. Founded in 1968 and U.S.-headquartered in Tempe, it is the largest Western packaging house and a strategic partner as the U.S. tries to bring advanced packaging onshore.

name: ASML
description: ASML is a Dutch maker of photolithography systems and the sole supplier of extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography — the machines required to make the most advanced chips. Founded in 1984 as a Philips/ASM joint venture in Veldhoven, it holds an effective monopoly at the leading edge, making it the single most strategically important equipment company and a focal point of export-control policy.

name: Applied Materials
description: Applied Materials is the largest semiconductor equipment company, supplying deposition, etch, ion implantation and CMP tools used across virtually every fab. Founded in 1967 in Santa Clara, it provides the broad toolset that turns blank wafers into patterned chips and is central to U.S. leverage over global manufacturing.

name: Lam Research
description: Lam Research specializes in etch, deposition and wafer-cleaning equipment, with particular strength in the 3D structures used for advanced memory and logic. Founded in 1980 by David Lam in Silicon Valley, it is one of the handful of firms whose tools are indispensable to NAND, DRAM and leading-edge logic fabs.

name: KLA
description: KLA is the dominant maker of process-control and metrology equipment — the inspection systems that find defects and keep fab yields high. Formed by the 1997 merger of KLA Instruments (founded 1975) and Tencor, it occupies a near-monopoly niche that grows more valuable as chips become more complex and defects more costly.

name: Tokyo Electron (TEL)
description: Tokyo Electron (TEL) is Japan's largest semiconductor equipment maker, supplying coater/developer (track), etch, deposition and cleaning systems. Founded in 1963 in Tokyo, it holds a near-monopoly in the coat/develop tools paired with ASML's lithography, making it a quiet but critical link in the leading-edge toolchain.

name: Foxconn (Hon Hai)
specialization: EMS, systems assembly, and select packaging
description: Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision Industry) is the world's largest electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider, assembling finished devices and increasingly moving into chip packaging and components. Founded in 1974 by Terry Gou in Taiwan, it built the giant China assembly complexes that produce much of the world's consumer electronics and is now diversifying into India, Vietnam and the U.S.

name: YMTC
description: Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC) is China's national champion in 3D NAND flash memory. Founded in 2016 in Wuhan with state backing, it advanced quickly with a novel stacking architecture before U.S. export controls in 2022 restricted its access to tools. It represents China's most credible bid for memory self-sufficiency.

name: CXMT (Innotron)
description: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is China's leading DRAM manufacturer. Founded in 2016 in Hefei, it is the country's main hope for domestic DRAM supply, ramping mature DRAM while facing the same export-control limits on advanced equipment that constrain the rest of China's industry.

name: Huawei / HiSilicon
specialization: Telecom and mobile SoC design (export-controlled leading-edge supply)
description: HiSilicon is the chip-design arm of Huawei, creating telecom, mobile (Kirin) and AI processors. Huawei was founded in 1987 in Shenzhen and built HiSilicon into a top fabless designer. Since 2020, U.S. sanctions have cut its access to TSMC and leading-edge tools, forcing reliance on SMIC and making it the central test case of China's chip resilience.
